messages:
support_jordan: FYI seeing a customer escalation — lots of 502/504s to hosted inference since ~03:20 UTC. Customers report requests hang then fail. Traces show Envoy upstream premature close and some TLS handshake timeouts to auth-service. Sample trace ids: trace=7f3a2b, 9d1c4e. Anyone on call?
ops-oncall: on it. Are these correlated with a deploy or traffic spike? :eyes:
support_jordan: no deploys around then per deploy-bot, traffic is +18% but nothing huge. Appears concentrated to auth-service ingress hosts (auth-v2).
sanjay: pulling logs now. Can you paste a sample curl we can run to repro?
support_jordan: repro curl that failed for customer: ```curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'``` Failure in client: "upstream premature close" after TLS handshake timeout.
mia: echoed in proxy logs: ```[2024-09-25T03:22:11Z] envoy upstream reset reason: TLS_HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT, envoy code: 0x7e``` Also seeing h2 stream resets from same source IPs.
ops-oncall: possible connection pool / keepalive exhaustion w/ TLS renegotiation on auth side. Any recent cert rotation?
sanjay: certs rotated yesterday but roll completed fine. However auth-service (auth-v2) started returning short-lived 401s while reloading keys — could be token backend churning.
infra-bot: automated alert: auth-v2 pod restarts increased by 30% between 03:10-03:25 UTC.
ops-oncall: that aligns. If auth instances are restarting, TLS sessions drop and Envoy could hit handshake timeout waiting for upstream to accept connections. We'll try routing traffic to auth-v1 fallback for a bit.
support_jordan: customers already complaining about latency and errors, opening a support ticket for top 3 affected customers. Notifying CS.
sanjay: quick mitigation: 1) add temporary host header route to auth-v1 (canary) 2) increase envoy upstream TLS handshake timeout to 20s for auth cluster 3) enable 5s retry with 1 retry on 502/504 for the gateway to reduce visible failures. I'll apply the routing change now.
mia: logs show a pattern: client TLS handshake succeeds, then backend TLS handshake times out when connecting to auth, so increasing handshake timeout helps but root cause is auth pod churn.
ops-oncall: applied route to auth-v1 for 10% traffic, updating to 50% now. Monitoring for error rate drop.
infra-bot: config change applied: route auth-cluster -> auth-v1 (50%).
support_jordan: error rates for affected customers dropped ~70% after routing shift. CS updated customers.
sanjay: next steps: 1) investigate why auth-v2 pods restarted (OOM or probe flaps?) 2) ensure graceful shutdown for TLS sessions or drain config 3) revert envoy timeout tweak after auth-v2 stable. Assign to eng-auth.
ops-oncall: looks like liveness probe misfire during a busy cert reload cycle; filed ENG-3142 and added initial notes.
dev-tools-bot: reminder: create postmortem if customer SLA impacted > 30m.
support_jordan: customer-impact window ~03:20-03:40 UTC (~20m). I'll start draft of escalation note and include traces/headers.
mia: any immediate config to prevent recurrence? Suggest we increase envoy upstream connection pool size and tune keepalive settings for auth cluster; also add jitter to cert reloads.
sanjay: agreed. I'll schedule follow-up with auth team to add graceful TLS reload and incremental rollouts.
ops-oncall: monitoring: I'll keep the fallback route for 1h then gradually revert once auth-v2 pod restarts drop to baseline.
support_jordan: thanks all. I'll paste the support ticket id and affected customer list here when created. :thumbsup:
